summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.1/76)

data.turoyo: B iḏoṯa gqayšo i zəbdo, yaʕni u məšḥo, i zəbdo, gmaləmola, gmašəġola w gəmmalḥola w gmaḥtola b səfoqo. <...>
data.translation: Mit den Händen schöpft sie die Butter ab, sammelt sie, wäscht sie, salzt sie und legt sie in ein Gefäß. <...>

rationale: New Infectum box; singular female agent and suffixed butter patient.

summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.1/83)

data.turoyo: I gwetaṯe kmašəġila, bəṯr məd hawyo, w kəmqaṭʕila, kəmmalḥila <...>
data.translation: Nachdem dieser Käse fertig ist, waschen sie ihn, schneiden ihn in Stücke und salzen ihn. <...>

rationale: Thin new Infectum cell; plural agent and cheese patient.

summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (JTM 1.1/83)

data.turoyo: <...> bəṯr mu məloḥawo ksaymila maye w malḥo, ġer manək, w kmaydi af falqani, kmaḥtənne b tanagaye w kkufxi i maye w malḥayo aʕlayye <...>
data.translation: <...> Nach dem Salzen machen sie zusätzlich eine Salzlake für ihn, nehmen die Stücke, legen sie in einen Blechkanister und gießen die Salzlake darüber. <...>

rationale: New Infinitiv box, provisionally classified; salting event in a temporal nominal phrase.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.26/1269)

data.turoyo: <...> Mmalḥiwo u baṣro. Mmalḥiwo kule b malḥo w tulanwole bag gawde <...>
data.translation: <...> They would salt the meat. They would salt all of it with salt, and they would store it in skins <...>

rationale: Infectum-wa/1 remains thin after round 1; explicit meat object and salt material in one coherent preservation sequence.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.26/1276)

data.turoyo: <...> Nəḥriwo ad darmala, ged mmalḥiwo u baṣro... <...>
data.translation: <...> They would slaughter the fattened animals, they would salt the meat... <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa/1: unusual ged plus -wo in a habitual recollection, preserved without changing morphology.

summary: The new Infectum forms are transitive: a feminine 3sg subject salts butter with suffix -la, and a 3pl subject salts cheese with -la. They supply the missing box beside the inherited Infectum-wa.
məloḥawo in bəṯr mu məloḥawo denotes the salting event and is provisionally placed in Infinitiv. -awo belongs to the nominal expression; it is not finite -wa.

The sequence in JTM 1.1/83 distinguishes salting the cheese from subsequently making and pouring a salt solution. It supports 'to salt'; no distinct sense 'to pickle' is inferred from the procedure or the inherited uncertain translation.

The inherited etymological question about direct verbal inheritance versus derivation from the salt noun remains open. The observed II morphology alone cannot decide historical derivation. No light-verb collocation of mlḥ is present.
All five occurrences reviewed. Round 1 Infectum and Infinitiv additions remain unchanged; new Jan material fills the still-thin Infectum-wa cell.
Mmalḥiwo has zero-marked u baṣro; the repeated predicate uses kule with material b malḥo. mmalḥiwole resumes meat by -le. mm- is the active II form here, not a Detransitive marker.
ged mmalḥiwo occurs inside repeated winter preparations; the prospective particle does not remove the source -wo or justify a separate box.
Jan 1.50/2439 overlaps the inherited QM 2461 quotation closely. Keep the existing reference pending crosswalk verification and do not double-count the example.

In Jan 4.I/516 water and contrast with yusqina favor a salty-state metaphor, but malxi cannot silently become malḥi. Lookup malxi finds mlx; mlx’s ruling sense does not fit the water contrast, yet that exclusion alone cannot prove mlḥ I. No new stem is published.
These records support salting, not a new pickling sense. No fixed light-verb idiom or new food-participant distinction is established; English remains supplied machine translation.
Confirm məloḥawo as the Infinitiv of II mmaləḥ rather than an independently derived action noun, and establish its base vocalism.
Can the inherited 'to pickle' gloss be supported by a separate context? These new records directly attest salting; they do not justify deleting the existing gloss.

Confirm source malxi at Jan 4.I/516: is x a transcription/phonetic variant of ḥ, and is the form Preterit Intransitive, Infectum or another state expression? Establish an I citation pair before creating the stem.
Does Jan 1.50/2439 correspond exactly to inherited QM 2461? Retain both citation systems until a verified crosswalk permits a reference correction.
Butter and cheese join the inherited meat patient. These food changes extend the same salting event, without a new sense.
